subject: science
passage: Leafcutter ants grow a fungus on chewed leaves in underground gardens, and this fungus is the colony's only food. Used leaf material, dead ants, and fungus infected by Escovopsis, a mold that attacks the gardens, are carried to separate waste heaps. Those heaps are tended by a small group of older workers that rarely, if ever, enter the gardens. Many entomologists think that this division of labor exists chiefly as a form of hygiene: by limiting contact with waste to a few workers who stay away from the fungus, the colony reduces the chance that mold spores will be carried back into its gardens.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the entomologists' explanation?

choices.A: When waste workers were allowed into some colonies' gardens, Escovopsis infections in those gardens rose.
choices.B: Older workers in a leafcutter colony cut and carry leaves less efficiently than younger workers do.
choices.C: Waste heaps contain far more Escovopsis spores than the fungus gardens or any other part of a leafcutter nest.
choices.D: Garden infection rates were the same whether or not waste workers had contact with the gardens.

explanation.why: The explanation is about the purpose of keeping waste workers away from the gardens: doing so should keep mold out. The strongest support would show what happens when that separation is removed. If gardens become more infected once waste workers are allowed in, the separation is protecting the gardens.
explanation.A: Correct. Removing the separation led to more mold in the gardens, which shows that the division of labor helps keep Escovopsis out.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This offers a different reason older ants might be given waste work, so it does not support the hygiene explanation.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This shows that waste is a likely source of spores, but not that keeping waste workers apart is what protects the gardens.
explanation.D: Incorrect. If contact with waste workers made no difference to infection, the hygiene explanation would be weakened.
